name: AMADEUS
full_name: ANTARES Modules for the Acoustic Detection Under the Sea
summary: An acoustic test system integrated into the ANTARES deep-sea neutrino telescope studied whether ultra-high-energy neutrino showers could be detected through their pressure pulses. It recorded data from 2008 to 2015.
detection_principle: Hydrophones and acoustic sensors in glass spheres record the thermo-acoustic pressure pulse that a compact particle shower could create in sea water. Correlations between sensors reconstruct transient directions and constrain ambient backgrounds.
technologies: Thermo-acoustic particle detection with hydrophones or piezoelectric sensors

sites.name: ANTARES site, approximately 40 km offshore Toulon, Mediterranean Sea
sites.location: ANTARES site, approximately 40 km offshore Toulon, Mediterranean Sea

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The official ANTARES acoustic page explicitly states that AMADEUS recorded data from 2008 to 2015.

timeline.event: Completed acoustic system began operation within ANTARES.
Detector description and initial in-situ performance published.

key_parameters.name: Acoustic channels
key_parameters.value: 36 sensors in six storeys, with six sensors per storey

key_parameters.name: Sensor spacings
key_parameters.value: About 1 m within a storey and distances up to 340 m between storeys

key_parameters.name: Depth
key_parameters.value: Approximately 2,050–2,300 m for acoustic sensors at the ANTARES site

results.summary: Measured ambient noise and transient acoustic backgrounds and demonstrated directional reconstruction. No confirmed acoustic-neutrino detection was reported.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
